title: Hopper FP8 stability tuning: degradation-sensitivity audit and rollback throttle
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Objective: Safely enable FP8 quantization profiles (E4M3 / E5M2) on Hopper GPUs by introducing a degradation-sensitivity audit, robust rollback-throttle mechanism, and a synthetic calibration harness that exercises per-op edge-cases. This ticket contains the engineering plan, validation criteria, and runbook changes required to complete a staged rollout across canaries -> limited production -> GA. The work aims to reduce oscillation during rollouts, avoid noisy flapping between FP8/INT8 modes, and ensure measurable accuracy regressions are caught and gated before impacting customers.
acceptance_criteria: Canary fleet (10% of nodes) runs FP8 profile with telemetry showing <0.5% downstream metric regression on golden prompt suite for 72 hours
Rollback-throttle prevents more than 2 automatic profile switches per model per hour to avoid oscillation
Synthetic calibration harness reproduces at least 90% of previously-observed activation drift cases seen in historical incidents
CI job 'quant-audit-hopper' passes with zero critical failures and reports per-op max quant error < threshold for 95% of layers
Runbook updated and on-call trained; emergency rollback can be executed in <15 minutes
tasks: Implement degradation-sensitivity detector: compute rolling median of eval-metric deltas over 30m and 6h windows
Add rollout throttle token bucket: limit automated FP8->fallback switches to 2 switches/hour/model
Extend calibration harness to synthesize long-tail sequences and out-of-distribution embedding ranges
Create CI job that runs quantized vs fp32 golden suite in emulated Hopper environment
Instrument per-op telemetry: l2-quant-residual, activation-tail-ratio, outlier-count
Author canary plan and update rollout policies in console (canary size, observation window, auto-fallback criteria)
Build dashboard panels: per-model regression rate, rollback events, throttle hits, and canary health
Document runbook steps and add JIRA/Slack alert runbooks for on-call
comments: 2026-02-11 Marco Chen: Spun up initial synthetic harness prototype. Early results show specific GELU variants have larger tail mass causing E4M3 to overflow quant buckets. Next: add tail trimming preprocessor and replay comparison.

2026-02-18 Lena Ortiz: PM review — prioritize dashboarding and auto-throttle; product requests a conservative default throttle of 1 switch/hour initially for GA but engineering recommends 2/hour for canaries. We'll do 2/hr for canaries and 1/hr for broader pools.

2026-02-24 QA: CI 'quant-audit-hopper' failing intermittently on the 'summarization-golden' prompt. Root cause: batch-order-dependent KV-caching difference when running quantized kernels. Ticketed ENG-47289 to add deterministic KV replay in the test harness.

2026-03-03 Reliability: Ran 48h canary with throttle disabled; observed 7 automatic switches across 6 models (oscillation). With throttle enabled (2/hr) oscillation reduced to 1-2 switches. Need hysteresis of 10m cooldown in addition to token bucket.
2026-03-09 Security: Reviewed telemetry payloads; confirmed no customer PII is sent. KMS integration unaffected. Security review required flag set on completion step.

2026-03-12 Marco Chen: Implemented cooldown hysteresis and updated dashboard. Preparing canary run for next maintenance window. Patching release candidate in runtime-1.24 branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2387
notes: Risk matrix included in design doc. Conservative rollout recommended for models with high downstream sensitivity (search ranking, summarization). For low-sensitivity models we can enable FP8 earlier if per-op telemetry is within thresholds. Follow-up tickets should convert observed thresholds into automated gating rules and backfill historical incidents into the synthetic harness dataset.
